One way drainage condition d=3m
For 90% consolidation
(Tv)90=Cv⋅t90d20.85=3×10−6×t90(3)2t90=0.85×93×10−6mint90=1770.83≃1771 days  \begin{aligned} \left(T_{v}\right)_{90} &=C_{v} \cdot \frac{t_{90}}{d^{2}} \\ 0.85 &=3 \times 10^{-6} \times \frac{t_{90}}{(3)^{2}} \\ t_{90} &=\frac{0.85 \times 9}{3 \times 10^{-6}} \mathrm{min} \\ t_{90} &=1770.83 \simeq 1771 \text { days } \end{aligned}(Tv​)90​0.85t90​t90​​=Cv​⋅d2t90​​=3×10−6×(3)2t90​​=3×10−60.85×9​min=1770.83≃1771 days ​
explanationText: As per Terzaghi's 1-D consolidation theory $T_{v}=C_{v} \frac{t}{d^{2}}$ One way drainage condition d=3m For 90% consolidation $\begin{aligned} \left(T_{v}\right)_{90} &=C_{v} \cdot \frac{t_{90}}{d^{2}} \\ 0.85 &=3 \times 10^{-6} \times \frac{t_{90}}{(3)^{2}} \\ t_{90} &=\frac{0.85 \times 9}{3 \times 10^{-6}} \mathrm{min} \\ t_{90} &=1770.83 \simeq 1771 \text { days } \end{aligned}$

explanationHtml:
Loss in strength of soil due to remoulding at same water content is termed as sensitivity.
Over a period of time soil regain a part of its lost strength is termed as thixotropy. When seepage takes place in upward direction, seepage pressure acts in upward direction and effective stress is reduced consequently shear strength is reduced.
In liquefaction, due to dynamic/cyclic loading in loose saturated sand, effective stress decreases and decrease in shear strength is recorded.
explanationText: Loss in strength of soil due to remoulding at same water content is termed as sensitivity. Over a period of time soil regain a part of its lost strength is termed as thixotropy. When seepage takes place in upward direction, seepage pressure acts in upward direction and effective stress is reduced consequently shear strength is reduced. In liquefaction, due to dynamic/cyclic loading in loose saturated sand, effective stress decreases and decrease in shear strength is recorded.

explanationText: $\begin{aligned} \text { Discharge } &=\frac{200 \mathrm{ml}}{15 \mathrm{min}} \\ &=\frac{200 \mathrm{cm}^{3}}{15 \times 60 \mathrm{sec}}=\frac{200 \times 10^{3}}{900} \frac{\mathrm{mm}^{3}}{\mathrm{sec}} \end{aligned}$ As per Darcy's Law, $\begin{aligned} q &=k_{a v g} i A \\ k_{a v g} &=\frac{\Sigma z_{i}}{\Sigma \frac{z_{i}}{k_{i}}}\\ &(\because\text{ flow is normal to bedding plane})\\ k_{\text {avg }}&=\frac{150+150}{\frac{150}{0.02}+\frac{150}{k}}\\ i&=\frac{\text { Head difference }}{\text { length }}=\frac{600-300}{300}=1 \\ A&=80 \mathrm{cm}^{2}=80 \times 10^{2} \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ q&=\left[\frac{150+150}{\frac{150}{0.02}+\frac{150}{k}}+\right] \times 1 \times 80 \times 10^{2} \\ &=\frac{200 \times 10^{3}}{900} \\ k&=0.045 \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \end{aligned}$

questionText: The porosity (n) and the degree of saturation (S) of a soil sample are 0.7 and 40%, respectively. In a 100 $m^{3}$ volume of the soil, the volume (expressed in $m^{3}$ ) of air is ________ .
explanationHtml: n=0.7.5=40%,V=100m3,Va=?n=VvV⇒0.7=Vv100⇒Vv=70m3 Now, S=VWVv=Vv−VaVv=1−VaVv⇒0.40=1−VaVv⇒VaVv=0.60⇒Va=0.6×70=42m3\begin{aligned} n=0.7 .5 &=40 \%, V=100 \mathrm{m}^{3}, V_{a}=? \\ n &=\frac{V_{v}}{V} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.7 &=\frac{V_{v}}{100} \\ \Rightarrow \quad V_{v} &=70 \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \text { Now, } \quad S &=\frac{V_{W}}{V_{v}}=\frac{V_{v}-V_{a}}{V_{v}}=1-\frac{V_{a}}{V_{v}}\\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.40&=1-\frac{V_{a}}{V_{v}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{V_{a}}{V_{v}}&=0.60 \Rightarrow V_{a}=0.6 \times 70=42 \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}n=0.7.5n⇒0.7⇒Vv​ Now, S⇒0.40⇒Vv​Va​​​=40%,V=100m3,Va​=?=VVv​​=100Vv​​=70m3=Vv​VW​​=Vv​Vv​−Va​​=1−Vv​Va​​=1−Vv​Va​​=0.60⇒Va​=0.6×70=42m3​

questionText: A pile of diameter 0.4 m is fully embedded in a clay stratum having 5 layers, each 5 m thick as shown in the figure below. Assume a constant unit weight of soil as 18 kN/ $m^{3}$ for all the layers. Using $\lambda$ -method ( $\lambda$ =0.15 for 25 m embedment length) and neglecting the end bearing component, the ultimate pile capacity (in kN) is ________.
explanationHtml:
Ultimate bearing capacity
=λ(σvav+2Cu)As=0.15[18×12.5+2Cu]×(π×0.4×25) \begin{aligned} &=\lambda\left(\sigma_{\mathrm{v} a v}+2 C_{u}\right) A_{s} \\ &=0.15\left[18 \times 12.5+2 C_{u}\right] \times(\pi \times 0.4 \times 25) \\ \end{aligned}​=λ(σvav​+2Cu​)As​=0.15[18×12.5+2Cu​]×(π×0.4×25)​
Cu C_{u}Cu​ is the average value of all layers i.e., 60 kPa.
=0.15[18×12.5+2×60]×(π×0.4×25)=1625.77kN \begin{aligned} &=0.15[18 \times 12.5+2 \times 60] \times(\pi \times 0.4 \times 25) \\ &=1625.77 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}​=0.15[18×12.5+2×60]×(π×0.4×25)=1625.77kN​
explanationText: Ultimate bearing capacity $\begin{aligned} &=\lambda\left(\sigma_{\mathrm{v} a v}+2 C_{u}\right) A_{s} \\ &=0.15\left[18 \times 12.5+2 C_{u}\right] \times(\pi \times 0.4 \times 25) \\ \end{aligned}$ $C_{u}$ is the average value of all layers i.e., 60 kPa. $\begin{aligned} &=0.15[18 \times 12.5+2 \times 60] \times(\pi \times 0.4 \times 25) \\ &=1625.77 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$

Vs=WsGsγwVs=16.2×500027×10m3=3000m3 \begin{aligned} V_{s} &=\frac{W_{s}}{G_{s} \gamma_{w}} \\ V_{s} &=\frac{16.2 \times 5000}{27 \times 10} \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ &=3000 \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}Vs​Vs​​=Gs​γw​Ws​​=27×1016.2×5000​m3=3000m3​

explanationHtml:

Vs=Vn V_{s}=\frac{V}{n}Vs​=nV​

n=VVV<1Hence,Vs>V \begin{aligned} n&=\frac{V_{V}}{V}<1 \\ \text{Hence,}\quad V_{s}&>V \end{aligned}nHence,Vs​​=VVV​​<1>V​
explanationText: Seepage velocity is given by $V_{s}=\frac{V}{n}$ where, V= discharge velocity $\begin{aligned} n&=\frac{V_{V}}{V}<1 \\ \text{Hence,}\quad V_{s}&>V \end{aligned}$

=qB(1−μ2)Es×If =\frac{q B\left(1-\mu^{2}\right)}{E_{s}} \times I_{f}=Es​qB(1−μ2)​×If​

questionText: Water is flowing at a steady rate through a homogeneous and saturated horizontal soil strip of 10 m length. The strip is being subjected to a constant water head(H) of 5 m at the beginning and 1 m at the end. If the governing equation of flow in the soil strip is $\frac{d^{2}H}{dx^2}=0$ (where x is the distance along the soil strip), the value of H (in m) at the middle of the strip is ________.
explanationHtml:
Given, equation of the flow of soil strip is
d2Hdx2=0⇒dHdx=C1⇒H=C1x+C2at x=0,H=5m⇒C2=5⇒H=C1x+5at x=10,H=1m⇒1=C1×10+5⇒10C1=−4⇒C1=−25⇒H=−25x+5at x=5mH=−25×5+5H=3m \begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2} H}{d x^{2}}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{d} x}&=\mathrm{C}_{1} \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=C_{1} x+C_{2} \\ \text{at }x=0, H=&5 \mathrm{m} \\ \Rightarrow \quad C_{2}&=5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=C_{1} x+5 \\ \text{at }x&=10, H=1 \mathrm{m} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1&=C_{1} \times 10+5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 10 C_{1}&=-4 \\ \Rightarrow \quad C_{1}&=-\frac{2}{5} \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=-\frac{2}{5} x+5 \\ \text{at }x&=5 \mathrm{m} \\ H&=-\frac{2}{5} \times 5+5 \\ H&=3 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}dx2d2H​⇒dxdH​⇒Hat x=0,H=⇒C2​⇒Hat x⇒1⇒10C1​⇒C1​⇒Hat xHH​=0=C1​=C1​x+C2​5m=5=C1​x+5=10,H=1m=C1​×10+5=−4=−52​=−52​x+5=5m=−52​×5+5=3m​
explanationText: Given, equation of the flow of soil strip is $\begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2} H}{d x^{2}}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{d} x}&=\mathrm{C}_{1} \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=C_{1} x+C_{2} \\ \text{at }x=0, H=&5 \mathrm{m} \\ \Rightarrow \quad C_{2}&=5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=C_{1} x+5 \\ \text{at }x&=10, H=1 \mathrm{m} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1&=C_{1} \times 10+5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 10 C_{1}&=-4 \\ \Rightarrow \quad C_{1}&=-\frac{2}{5} \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=-\frac{2}{5} x+5 \\ \text{at }x&=5 \mathrm{m} \\ H&=-\frac{2}{5} \times 5+5 \\ H&=3 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$

explanationText: $\begin{aligned} e_{max} &=0.85 \\ e_{min} &=0.5 \\ \rho_{\text {field }} &=1800 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}\\ &\text{at water content }=8\% \\ \rho_{w}&=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ G_{S}&=2.7 \end{aligned}$ Relative density, $\mathrm{I}_{D}=?$ $\begin{aligned} \rho=\frac{G_{p_{W}}(1+w)}{1+e}&=\frac{2.7 \times 1000(1.08)}{1+e}\\ \Rightarrow\quad 1+e &=\frac{2.7 \times 1000 \times 1.08}{1800} \\ \Rightarrow\quad e &=0.62\\ \Rightarrow\quad I_{D} &=\frac{e_{\max }-e}{e_{\max }-e_{\min }} \times 100 \\ &=\frac{0.85-0.62}{0.85-0.5} \times 100 \\ &=65.714 \% \end{aligned}$

explanationText: Load on each column =400 kN Bearing capacity of soil $=100 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ $\therefore \quad$ Area of each footing required $\begin{aligned} &=\frac{400}{100} m^{2}=4 m^{2}\\ \therefore \quad \text{Total area required } &=4 \times 4=16 \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \therefore \quad \frac{\text { Foundation area }}{\text { Plot area }}&=\frac{16}{100}=16 \% \end{aligned}$ If the foundation area is less than 40% of plot area, then isolated foundation is suitable otherwise provide raft foundation or combined footing.

questionText: In its natural condition, a soil sample has a mass of 1.980 kg and a volume of 0.001 $m^{3}$ . After being completely dried in an oven, the mass of the sample is 1.800 kg. Specific gravity G is 2.7. Unit weight of water is 10 kN/ $m^{3}$ . The degree of saturation of the soil is:
explanationHtml: ρ=MV=1.9800.001=1980kg/m3ρd=MdV=1.8000.001=1800kg/m3ρd=ρ1+w⇒1800=19801+w⇒w=0.1∵ρd=G⋅ρw1+e⇒1800=2.7×10001+e⇒e=0.5∵wG=e.s⇒0.1×2.7=0.5S⇒S=0.54\begin{aligned} \rho &=\frac{M}{V} \\ &=\frac{1.980}{0.001}=1980 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \rho_{d} &=\frac{M_{d}}{V}\\ &=\frac{1.800}{0.001}=1800 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \rho_{d} &=\frac{\rho}{1+\mathrm{w}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1800 &=\frac{1980}{1+\mathrm{w}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \mathrm{w}=0.1 \\ \because \quad & \rho_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{G} \cdot \rho_{\mathrm{w}}}{1+\mathrm{e}}\\ \Rightarrow \quad 1800&=\frac{2.7 \times 1000}{1+e} \\ \Rightarrow \quad e&=0.5 \\ \because wG&=e.s\\ \Rightarrow 0.1 \times 2.7&=0.5 S \\ \Rightarrow \quad S&=0.54 \end{aligned}ρρd​ρd​⇒1800⇒∵⇒1800⇒e∵wG⇒0.1×2.7⇒S​=VM​=0.0011.980​=1980kg/m3=VMd​​=0.0011.800​=1800kg/m3=1+wρ​=1+w1980​w=0.1ρd​=1+eG⋅ρw​​=1+e2.7×1000​=0.5=e.s=0.5S=0.54​
explanationText: $\begin{aligned} \rho &=\frac{M}{V} \\ &=\frac{1.980}{0.001}=1980 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \rho_{d} &=\frac{M_{d}}{V}\\ &=\frac{1.800}{0.001}=1800 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \rho_{d} &=\frac{\rho}{1+\mathrm{w}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1800 &=\frac{1980}{1+\mathrm{w}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \mathrm{w}=0.1 \\ \because \quad & \rho_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{G} \cdot \rho_{\mathrm{w}}}{1+\mathrm{e}}\\ \Rightarrow \quad 1800&=\frac{2.7 \times 1000}{1+e} \\ \Rightarrow \quad e&=0.5 \\ \because wG&=e.s\\ \Rightarrow 0.1 \times 2.7&=0.5 S \\ \Rightarrow \quad S&=0.54 \end{aligned}$

questionText: An embankment is to be constructed with a granular soil (bulk unit weight = 20 kN/ $m^3$ ) on a saturated clayey silt deposit (undrained shear strength = 25 kPa). Assuming undrained general shear failure and bearing capacity factor of 5.7, the maximum height (in m) of the embankment at the point of failure is
explanationHtml:
Given, γ=20kN/m3\gamma=20 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} γ=20kN/m3
Shear strength s=25kN/m2\mathrm{s}=25 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} s=25kN/m2
Bearing capacity factor, Nc=5.7N_{c}=5.7 Nc​=5.7
∵=c⇒c=25kN/m2qu=cNc=25×5.7⇒γDt=25×5.7⇒D1=7.1m \begin{aligned} \because\quad &=c \quad \Rightarrow c=25 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ q_{u}&=c N_{c}=25 \times 5.7 \\ \Rightarrow \gamma \mathrm{D}_{t}&=25 \times 5.7\\ \Rightarrow \quad D_{1}&=7.1 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}∵qu​⇒γDt​⇒D1​​=c⇒c=25kN/m2=cNc​=25×5.7=25×5.7=7.1m​
explanationText: Given, $\gamma=20 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ Shear strength $\mathrm{s}=25 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ Bearing capacity factor, $N_{c}=5.7$ $\begin{aligned} \because\quad &=c \quad \Rightarrow c=25 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ q_{u}&=c N_{c}=25 \times 5.7 \\ \Rightarrow \gamma \mathrm{D}_{t}&=25 \times 5.7\\ \Rightarrow \quad D_{1}&=7.1 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$

questionText: A sand layer found at sea floor under 20 m water depth is characterized with relative density=40%, maximum void ratio=1.0 , minimum void ratio=0.5, and specific gravity of soil solids=2.67. Assume the specific gravity of sea water to be 1.03 and the unit weight of fresh water to be 9.81 kN/ $m^3$ . What would be the change in the effective stress (rounded off to the nearest integer value of kPa) at 30 m depth into the sand layer if the sea water level permanently rises by 2m?
explanationHtml:
The effective stress will not alter due to change in sea water level. The total stress will increase due to increase in sea water level. The pore water pressure will also increase in the same proportion, thus nullifying the effect of each other

The pore water pressure will also increase in the same proportion, thus nullifying the effect of each other $\begin{aligned} \sigma &=22 \times 10.1043+30 \times 19.48 \\ &=806.695 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ u &=(22+30) \times 10.1043 \\ &=525.424 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \therefore\quad \bar{\sigma} &=\sigma-u=806.695-525.424 \\ &=281.271 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$

questionText: A sand layer found at sea floor under 20 m water depth is characterized with relative density=40%, maximum void ratio=1.0 , minimum void ratio=0.5, and specific gravity of soil solids=2.67. Relative density is given by
ID(%)=(emax⁡−enat emax⁡−emin⁡)×100⇒40=(1−enat1−0.5)×100⇒0.4×0.5=1−enat ⇒enat =0.8Also,Gsea =γsea γw⇒γsea =1.03×9.81⇒γsea=10.1043kN/m3 \begin{aligned} I_{D}(\%)&=\left(\frac{e_{\max }-e_{\text {nat }}}{e_{\max }-e_{\min }}\right) \times 100\\ \Rightarrow \quad 40&=\left(\frac{1-e_{n a t}}{1-0.5}\right) \times 100 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.4 \times 0.5&=1-e_{\text {nat }} \\ \Rightarrow \quad e_{\text {nat }}&=0.8 \\ \text{Also,} \quad G_{\text {sea }}&=\frac{\gamma_{\text {sea }}}{\gamma_{w}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \gamma_{\text {sea }}&=1.03 \times 9.81 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \gamma_{\mathrm{sea}}&=10.1043 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \end{aligned}ID​(%)⇒40⇒0.4×0.5⇒enat ​Also,Gsea ​⇒γsea ​⇒γsea​​=(emax​−emin​emax​−enat ​​)×100=(1−0.51−enat​​)×100=1−enat ​=0.8=γw​γsea ​​=1.03×9.81=10.1043kN/m3​

γsat=(Gγsea+Senat ×γsea 1+enat )=(2.67×10.1043+1×0.8×10.10431+0.8)=19.48kN/m3\begin{aligned} \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}&=\left(\frac{G \gamma_{sea}+\mathrm{Se}_{\text {nat }} \times \gamma_{\text {sea }}}{1+e_{\text {nat }}}\right)\\ &=\left(\frac{2.67 \times 10.1043 +1 \times 0.8 \times 10.1043}{1+0.8}\right) \\ &=19.48 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}γsat​​=(1+enat ​Gγsea​+Senat ​×γsea ​​)=(1+0.82.67×10.1043+1×0.8×10.1043​)=19.48kN/m3​
Total stress at the bottom of sand layer,
σ=20×γsen⁡+30×γsat=20×10.1043+30×19.48=786.486kN/m2 \begin{aligned} \sigma &=20 \times \gamma_{\operatorname{sen}}+30 \times \gamma_{\text {sat}} \\ &=20 \times 10.1043+30 \times 19.48 \\ &=786.486 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}σ​=20×γsen​+30×γsat​=20×10.1043+30×19.48=786.486kN/m2​
Pore water pressure at the bottom of sand layer,
u=(20+30)×10.1043=505.215kN/m2 \begin{aligned} u &=(20+30) \times 10.1043 \\ &=505.215 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}u​=(20+30)×10.1043=505.215kN/m2​
Effective stress at the bottom of sand layer.
σˉ=σ−u=786.486−505.215=281.271kN/m2 \begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma} &=\sigma-u=786.486 -505.215 \\ &=281.271 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}σˉ​=σ−u=786.486−505.215=281.271kN/m2​

The silty clay layers at X and Y are identical. The thin sand layer at Y is continuous and freedraining with a very large discharge capacity. If primary consolidation at X is estimated to complete in 36 months, what would be the corresponding time for completion of primary consolidation at Y ?
questionText: Identical surcharges are placed at ground surface at sites X and Y , with soil conditions shown in figure and water table at ground surface. The silty clay layers at X and Y are identical. The thin sand layer at Y is continuous and freedraining with a very large discharge capacity. If primary consolidation at X is estimated to complete in 36 months, what would be the corresponding time for completion of primary consolidation at Y ?
explanationHtml:
The time required for any degree of consolidation can be obtained from the Taylor's formula,
Tv=Cvtd2 T_{v}=\frac{C_{v} t}{d^{2}}Tv​=d2Cv​t​
since C_{v} is constant for same type of soil and TvT_{v} Tv​ is constant for same degree of consolidation,
t∝d2 t \propto d^{2} t∝d2 where d is the length of drainage path.
t1t2=(d1d2)2⇒36t2=(1010/2)2⇒t2=364⇒t2=9  months \begin{aligned} \frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}&=\left(\frac{d_{1}}{d_{2}}\right)^{2}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{36}{t_{2}}&=\left(\frac{10}{10 / 2}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t_{2}&=\frac{36}{4} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t_{2}&=9 \;\text{months} \end{aligned}t2​t1​​⇒t2​36​⇒t2​⇒t2​​=(d2​d1​​)2=(10/210​)2=436​=9months​
explanationText: The time required for any degree of consolidation can be obtained from the Taylor's formula, $T_{v}=\frac{C_{v} t}{d^{2}}$ since C_{v} is constant for same type of soil and $T_{v}$ is constant for same degree of consolidation, $t \propto d^{2}$ where d is the length of drainage path. $\begin{aligned} \frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}&=\left(\frac{d_{1}}{d_{2}}\right)^{2}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{36}{t_{2}}&=\left(\frac{10}{10 / 2}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t_{2}&=\frac{36}{4} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t_{2}&=9 \;\text{months} \end{aligned}$

questionText: A singly under-reamed, 8 m long, RCC pile (shown in the figure) weighing 20 kN with 350 mm shaft diameter and 750 mm under-ream diameter is installed within stiff, saturated silty clay (undrained shear strength is 50 kPa, adhesion factor is 0.3, and the applicable bearing capacity factor is 9) to counteract the impact of soil swelling on a structure constructed above. Neglecting suction and the contribution of the under-ream to the adhesive shaft capacity, what would be the estimated ultimate tensile capacity (rounded off to the nearest integer value of kN) of the pile?
explanationHtml:
The tensile resistance of a pile is given as
Qt=Qs+W+QbWhereQs= shaft resistance =αcAsW= weight of pile Q1=cNcAb∴Q1=αcAs+W+cNcAb=0.3×50×π×0.35×8+20+50×9×π(0.752−0.352)4=300.796kN \begin{aligned} Q_{t} &=Q_{s}+W+Q_{b} \\ \text{Where}\quad Q_{s} &=\text { shaft resistance }=\alpha c A_{s} \\ W &=\text { weight of pile } \\ Q_{1} &=c N_{c} A_{b} \\ \therefore \quad Q_{1} &=\alpha c A_{s}+W+c N_{c} A_{b} \\ &=0.3 \times 50 \times \pi \times 0.35 \times 8+20 \\ &+\frac{50 \times 9 \times \pi\left(0.75^{2}-0.35^{2}\right)}{4} \\ &=300.796 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}Qt​WhereQs​WQ1​∴Q1​​=Qs​+W+Qb​= shaft resistance =αcAs​= weight of pile =cNc​Ab​=αcAs​+W+cNc​Ab​=0.3×50×π×0.35×8+20+450×9×π(0.752−0.352)​=300.796kN​
explanationText: The tensile resistance of a pile is given as $\begin{aligned} Q_{t} &=Q_{s}+W+Q_{b} \\ \text{Where}\quad Q_{s} &=\text { shaft resistance }=\alpha c A_{s} \\ W &=\text { weight of pile } \\ Q_{1} &=c N_{c} A_{b} \\ \therefore \quad Q_{1} &=\alpha c A_{s}+W+c N_{c} A_{b} \\ &=0.3 \times 50 \times \pi \times 0.35 \times 8+20 \\ &+\frac{50 \times 9 \times \pi\left(0.75^{2}-0.35^{2}\right)}{4} \\ &=300.796 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$

explanationHtml:

explanationText: The ultimate bearing capacity of a square footing in clay as per Terzaghi's bearing capacity equation is given by, $\begin{aligned} q_{\mathrm{ult}} &=1.3 \mathrm{cN}_{c}\left[\because N_{c} \text { for clay }=5.7\right] \\ &=1.3 \times 27 \times 5.7=200 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}$

questionText: The ultimate load capacity of a 10 m long concrete pile of square cross section 500mm x 500 mm driven into a homogeneous clay layer having undrained cohesion value of 40 kPa is 700 kN. If the cross section of the pile is reduced to 250mm x 2500 mm and the length of the pile is increased to 20 m, the ultimate load capacity will be
explanationHtml:
The ultimate load of a pile in clay is given by,
Qu=cNAb+αcAs⇒700=40×9×0.5×0.5+α×40×0.5×4×10⇒α=0.7625 Again, Qu=40×9×0.25×0.25+0.7625×40×0.25×4×20Qu=632.5kN \begin{aligned} Q_{u}=& c N A_{b}+\alpha c A_{s} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 700=& 40 \times 9 \times 0.5 \times 0.5+\alpha \times 40 \\ & \times 0.5 \times 4 \times 10 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \alpha&=0.7625 \\ \text { Again, } \quad Q_{u}=& 40 \times 9 \times 0.25 \times 0.25+0.7625 \times 40 \\ & \times 0.25 \times 4 \times 20 \\ Q_{u} &=632.5 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}Qu​=⇒700=⇒α Again, Qu​=Qu​​cNAb​+αcAs​40×9×0.5×0.5+α×40×0.5×4×10=0.762540×9×0.25×0.25+0.7625×40×0.25×4×20=632.5kN​
explanationText: The ultimate load of a pile in clay is given by, $\begin{aligned} Q_{u}=& c N A_{b}+\alpha c A_{s} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 700=& 40 \times 9 \times 0.5 \times 0.5+\alpha \times 40 \\ & \times 0.5 \times 4 \times 10 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \alpha&=0.7625 \\ \text { Again, } \quad Q_{u}=& 40 \times 9 \times 0.25 \times 0.25+0.7625 \times 40 \\ & \times 0.25 \times 4 \times 20 \\ Q_{u} &=632.5 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$

questionText: A fine grained soil has liquid limit of 60 and plastic limit of 20. As per the plasticity chart, according to IS classification, the soil is represented by the letter symbols
explanationHtml:
Plasticity index.
Ip=wL−wp=60−20=40 \begin{aligned} I_{p} &=w_{L}-w_{p} \\ &=60-20=40 \end{aligned}Ip​​=wL​−wp​=60−20=40​
Equation of A line is given by
Ip=0.73(wL−20)=0.73(60−20)=292 \begin{aligned} I_{p} &=0.73\left(w_{L}-20\right) \\ &=0.73(60-20) \\ &=292 \end{aligned}Ip​​=0.73(wL​−20)=0.73(60−20)=292​
Thus the given soil lies above the A-Line. The liquid limit of the soil is more than 50 , hence the soil will be CH.

questionText: In a compaction test, G, w, S and e represent the specific gravity, water content, degree of saturation and void ratio of the soil sample, respectively. If $\gamma _{w}$ represents the unit weight of water and $\gamma _{d}$ represents the dry unit weight of the soil, the equation of zero air voids line is

options.html: γd=Gγw1+Se\gamma _{d}=\frac{G\gamma _{w}}{1+Se}γd​=1+SeGγw​​
γd=Gγw1+Gw\gamma _{d}=\frac{G\gamma _{w}}{1+Gw}γd​=1+GwGγw​​
γd=Gwe+γwS\gamma _{d}=\frac{Gw}{e+\gamma _{w}S}γd​=e+γw​SGw​
γd=Gw1+Se\gamma _{d}=\frac{Gw}{1+Se}γd​=1+SeGw​

explanationHtml:
The bulk unit weight of soil is given by
γ=(G+Se)γw1+e \gamma=\frac{(G+S e) \gamma_{w}}{1+e}γ=1+e(G+Se)γw​​
For dry unit weight, degree of saturation,
S=0∴γd=Gγw1+e S=0 \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+e}S=0∴γd​=1+eGγw​​
But we know that
Gw= Se ∴γd=Gγw1+GwS G w=\text { Se } \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+\frac{G w}{S}}Gw= Se ∴γd​=1+SGw​Gγw​​
For zero air voids, degree of saturation,
S=100%∴γd=Gγw1+Gw S=100 \% \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+G w}S=100%∴γd​=1+GwGγw​​
explanationText: The bulk unit weight of soil is given by $\gamma=\frac{(G+S e) \gamma_{w}}{1+e}$ For dry unit weight, degree of saturation, $S=0 \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+e}$ But we know that $G w=\text { Se } \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+\frac{G w}{S}}$ For zero air voids, degree of saturation, $S=100 \% \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+G w}$

Fine grained soils are those having 50% or more pass through 75μ\muμ sieve (0.075 mm). It is designated as sand (S) if 50% or more pass through 4.75 mm sieve otherwise designated as gravel (G).

The point corresponding to wL=35w_L=35 %wL​=35 and IP=8I_P=8 %IP​=8 lies below A- line on the Plasticity chart. It is designated as M or O.
Therefore, the soil is classified as SM.

questionText: The ground conditions at a site are as shown in the figure. The water table at the site which was initially at a depth of 5 m below the ground level got permanently lowered to a depth of 15 m below the ground level due to pumping of water over a few years. Assume the following data : I unit weight of water= 10 $kN/m^{3}$ II unit weight of sand above water table= 18 $kN/m^{3}$ III unit weight of sand and clay below the water table= 20 $kN/m^{3}$ IV coefficient of volume compressibility= 0.25 $m^{2}$ /MN What is the change in the effective stress in $kN/m^{2}$ at mid-depth of the clay layer due to the lowering of the water table ?
explanationHtml:
Initial total, pore and effective stresses at central layer are
σc−c=5×18+15×20+2.5×20=440kN/m2uc−c=(15+2−5)×10=175kN/m2(σ′)1=265kN/m2 \begin{aligned} \sigma_{c-c} &=5 \times 18+15 \times 20+2.5 \times 20 \\ &=440 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ u_{c-c} &=(15+2-5) \times 10=175 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \left(\sigma^{\prime}\right)_{1}=& 265 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}σc−c​uc−c​(σ′)1​=​=5×18+15×20+2.5×20=440kN/m2=(15+2−5)×10=175kN/m2265kN/m2​
After the drawdown of GWT, changes in total and pore pressure at central layer are as follows
σc−c=15×18+5×20+2.5×20=420kN/m2uc−c=7.5×10=75kN/m2(σ)2=345kN/m2⇒Δσ′=345−265Δσ′=80kN/m2 \begin{aligned} \sigma_{c-c}&=15 \times 18+5 \times 20+2.5 \times 20 \\ &=420 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} & \\ &\begin{aligned} u_{c-c}&=7.5 \times 10=75 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ (\sigma)_{2}&=345 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \Delta \sigma^{\prime}&=345-265 \\ \Delta \sigma^{\prime}&=80 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}σc−c​​=15×18+5×20+2.5×20=420kN/m2uc−c​(σ)2​⇒Δσ′Δσ′​=7.5×10=75kN/m2=345kN/m2=345−265=80kN/m2​​
explanationText: Initial total, pore and effective stresses at central layer are $\begin{aligned} \sigma_{c-c} &=5 \times 18+15 \times 20+2.5 \times 20 \\ &=440 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ u_{c-c} &=(15+2-5) \times 10=175 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \left(\sigma^{\prime}\right)_{1}=& 265 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$ After the drawdown of GWT, changes in total and pore pressure at central layer are as follows $\begin{aligned} \sigma_{c-c}&=15 \times 18+5 \times 20+2.5 \times 20 \\ &=420 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} & \\ &\begin{aligned} u_{c-c}&=7.5 \times 10=75 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ (\sigma)_{2}&=345 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \Delta \sigma^{\prime}&=345-265 \\ \Delta \sigma^{\prime}&=80 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$

questionMarkup: The bearing capacity of a rectangular footing of plan dimensions 1.5m x 3m resting on the surface of a sand deposit was estimated as 600 kN/m2m^{2}m2 when the water table is far below the base of the footing. The bearing capacities in kN/m2m^{2}m2 when the water level rises to depths of 3 m, 1.5 m and 0.5 m below the base of the footing are
questionText: The bearing capacity of a rectangular footing of plan dimensions 1.5m x 3m resting on the surface of a sand deposit was estimated as 600 kN/ $m^{2}$ when the water table is far below the base of the footing. The bearing capacities in kN/ $m^{2}$ when the water level rises to depths of 3 m, 1.5 m and 0.5 m below the base of the footing are
explanationHtml:
The bearing capacity of the sand deposit will remain same until the water table rises to a depth less than the width of the footing. Thus, when water table is 3.0 below footing, the bearing capacity is 600kN/m2600 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}600kN/m2;
similarly when water table is 1.5m below footing, the bearing capacity remaining same i.e. 600kN/m2600 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}600kN/m2.
But when the water table rises to a depth of 0.5m below the footing, the sand deposit will be saturated for a depth of 1.5-0.5=1m. Thus, the bearing capacity below the base of footing will decrease due to submergence of soil (1m).
explanationText: The bearing capacity of the sand deposit will remain same until the water table rises to a depth less than the width of the footing. Thus, when water table is 3.0 below footing, the bearing capacity is $600 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ ; similarly when water table is 1.5m below footing, the bearing capacity remaining same i.e. $600 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ . But when the water table rises to a depth of 0.5m below the footing, the sand deposit will be saturated for a depth of 1.5-0.5=1m. Thus, the bearing capacity below the base of footing will decrease due to submergence of soil (1m).

questionText: List-I below gives the possible types of failure for a finite soil slope and List-II gives the reasons for these different types of failure. Match the items in List-I with the items in List-II
explanationHtml:
Face failure or slope failure can occur when the Slope angle β \beta β is very high and the soil close to the toe is quite strong or the soil in the upper part of slope is relatively weak.
Base failure can occur when the soil below the toe is relatively weak and soft and the slope is flat.
Toe failure occurs in steep slopes when the soil mass above the base and below the base is homogeneous.
explanationText: Face failure or slope failure can occur when the Slope angle $\beta$ is very high and the soil close to the toe is quite strong or the soil in the upper part of slope is relatively weak. Base failure can occur when the soil below the toe is relatively weak and soft and the slope is flat. Toe failure occurs in steep slopes when the soil mass above the base and below the base is homogeneous.

questionText: The range of void ratio between which quick sand condition occurs in cohesionless granular soil deposits is
explanationHtml:
The specific gravity of cohesionless granular soils (sands) does not vary much and for all practical purposes it is taken to be 2.65. Critical hydraulic gradient should be nearly 1 for quick sand condition.
i.e.icr=G−11+e i.e.\quad i_{cr}=\frac{G-1}{1+e} i.e.icr​=1+eG−1​
From the above equation, the void ratio range is found to be between 0.6 and 0.7.

questionText: Negative skin friction in a soil is considered when the pile is constructed through
explanationHtml: Negative skin friction is experienced when the soil around the pile settles at a faster rate than pile. Thus, piles installed in freshly prepared fills of soft compressive deposits are subject to a downward drag. This downward drag on the pile surface, where the soil moves down relative to the pile, adds to the structural loads and is called negative skin friction.

questionText: A 6 m thick clay layer undergoes 90% consolidation four times faster under two-way drainage as compared to one-way drainage. In an identical clay layer of 15 m thickness, two-way drainage will be faster as compared to one-way drainage by
explanationHtml:
The time required for any degree of consolidation, can be obtained from the Taylor's formula
Tv=Cvtd2 T_{v}=\frac{C_{v} t}{d^{2}}Tv​=d2Cv​t​
Now, CvC_{v}Cv​ is constant for same type of soils, TvT_{v}Tv​ will also remain constant for same degree of consolidation. Thus, t \propto d^{2} where d is length of drainage path.
Hence, in the clay layer of 15m thickness, two way drainage will be four times faster in comparison to one way drainage.

questionText: A 10 m thick clay layer is underlain by a sand layer of 20 m depth (see figure below). The water table is 5 m below the surface of clay layer. The soil above the water table is capillary saturated. The value of $\gamma _{sat}$ is 19 kN/ $m^{3}$ . The unit weight of water is $\gamma _{w}$ . decrease by 10γw10\gamma _{w}10γw​

explanationHtml:
In first case, when the water table is 5m below the surface and the clay over water table is capillary saturated, the effective stress is given by
σˉ1=γsat ×5+γ×5=γsat ×5+(γsat −γw)×5⇒σˉ1=10γsat −5γw      …(i) \begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{1} &=\gamma_{\text {sat }} \times 5+\gamma \times 5 \\ &=\gamma_{\text {sat }} \times 5+\left(\gamma_{\text {sat }}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \times 5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \bar{\sigma}_{1} &=10 \gamma_{\text {sat }}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \; \; \; \ldots(i) \end{aligned}σˉ1​⇒σˉ1​​=γsat ​×5+γ×5=γsat ​×5+(γsat ​−γw​)×5=10γsat ​−5γw​…(i)​
In the second case, when water table rises to the surface, the effective stress is given by
σˉ2=γ×10=(γsat −γw)×10=10γsat −10γw=(10γsat−5γw)−5γw[∵ from (i) )⇒σˉ2=σˉ1−5γw\begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{2} &=\gamma \times 10=\left(\gamma_{\text {sat }}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \times 10 \\ &=10 \gamma_{\text {sat }}-10 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \\ &=\left(10 \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right)-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \quad[\because \text { from (i) }) \\ \Rightarrow \bar{\sigma}_{2} &=\bar{\sigma}_{1}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \end{aligned}σˉ2​⇒σˉ2​​=γ×10=(γsat ​−γw​)×10=10γsat ​−10γw​=(10γsat​−5γw​)−5γw​[∵ from (i) )=σˉ1​−5γw​​
Thus in second case, the effective stress at the interface will decrease by 5γw5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}5γw​.
explanationText: In first case, when the water table is 5m below the surface and the clay over water table is capillary saturated, the effective stress is given by $\begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{1} &=\gamma_{\text {sat }} \times 5+\gamma \times 5 \\ &=\gamma_{\text {sat }} \times 5+\left(\gamma_{\text {sat }}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \times 5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \bar{\sigma}_{1} &=10 \gamma_{\text {sat }}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \; \; \; \ldots(i) \end{aligned}$ In the second case, when water table rises to the surface, the effective stress is given by $\begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{2} &=\gamma \times 10=\left(\gamma_{\text {sat }}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \times 10 \\ &=10 \gamma_{\text {sat }}-10 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \\ &=\left(10 \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right)-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \quad[\because \text { from (i) }) \\ \Rightarrow \bar{\sigma}_{2} &=\bar{\sigma}_{1}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \end{aligned}$ Thus in second case, the effective stress at the interface will decrease by $5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}$ .

explanationHtml:
Even if there is a sudden drawdown of water in the canal, the soil remains saturated for sometime. Hence, unit weight of the soil will be the saturated unit weight i.e.
γsat =γ+γw=8.09+9.81=17.9kN/m3 \begin{aligned} \gamma_{\text {sat }} &=\gamma+\gamma_{w}=8.09+9.81 \\ &=17.9 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}γsat ​​=γ+γw​=8.09+9.81=17.9kN/m3​

questionText: A braced cut, 5 m wide and 7.5 m deep is proposed in a cohesionless soil deposit having effective cohesion c'=0 and effective friction angle, ${\phi}' =36^{\circ}$ . The first row of struts is to be installed at a depth of 0.5 m below ground surface and spacing between the struts should be 1.5 m. If the horizontal spacing of struts is 3 m and unit weight of the deposit is 20 $kN/m^{3}$ , the maximum strut load will be
explanationHtml:
Ka=1−sin⁡ϕ′1+sin⁡ϕ′=1−sin⁡36∘1+sin⁡36∘=0.2596\begin{aligned} K_{a} &=\frac{1-\sin \phi^{\prime}}{1+\sin \phi^{\prime}} \\ &=\frac{1-\sin 36^{\circ}}{1+\sin 36^{\circ}}=0.2596 \end{aligned}Ka​​=1+sinϕ′1−sinϕ′​=1+sin36∘1−sin36∘​=0.2596​
∴ \therefore∴ Uniform pressure on side of cut
=0.65KaγH=0.65×0.2596×20×7.5=25.31kN/m2 \begin{aligned} &=0.65 \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}} \gamma \mathrm{H} \\ &=0.65 \times 0.2596 \times 20 \times 7.5 \\ &=25.31 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}​=0.65Ka​γH=0.65×0.2596×20×7.5=25.31kN/m2​
Area covered by strut
1=3×(0.5+0.75)=3.75m2 \begin{aligned} 1 &=3 \times(0.5+0.75) \\ &=3.75 \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}1​=3×(0.5+0.75)=3.75m2​
Area covered by strut 2 and downward struts
=3×(0.75+0.75)=4.5m2 =3 \times(0.75+0.75)=4.5 \mathrm{m}^{2}=3×(0.75+0.75)=4.5m2
∴ \therefore ∴ Maximum force will be carried by strut
2 and downward struts
=25.31×4.5=113.89kN≃113.90kN \begin{aligned} &=25.31 \times 4.5=113.89 \mathrm{kN} \\ &\simeq 113.90 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}​=25.31×4.5=113.89kN≃113.90kN​
explanationText: $\begin{aligned} K_{a} &=\frac{1-\sin \phi^{\prime}}{1+\sin \phi^{\prime}} \\ &=\frac{1-\sin 36^{\circ}}{1+\sin 36^{\circ}}=0.2596 \end{aligned}$ $\therefore$ Uniform pressure on side of cut $\begin{aligned} &=0.65 \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}} \gamma \mathrm{H} \\ &=0.65 \times 0.2596 \times 20 \times 7.5 \\ &=25.31 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$ Area covered by strut $\begin{aligned} 1 &=3 \times(0.5+0.75) \\ &=3.75 \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$ Area covered by strut 2 and downward struts $=3 \times(0.75+0.75)=4.5 \mathrm{m}^{2}$ $\therefore$ Maximum force will be carried by strut 2 and downward struts $\begin{aligned} &=25.31 \times 4.5=113.89 \mathrm{kN} \\ &\simeq 113.90 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$

For embankment compaction, the volume of soil covered by rammer
=0.05×104×50010=25000cc \begin{aligned} &=0.05 \times 10^{4} \times \frac{500}{10} \\ &=25000 \mathrm{cc} \end{aligned}​=0.05×104×10500​=25000cc​

questionText: A granular soil possesses saturated density of 20 $kN/m^{3}$ . Its effective angle of internal friction is 35 degrees. If the desired factor of safety is 1.5, the safe angle of slope for this soil, when seepage occurs at and parallel to the slope surface, will be

20∘^{\circ}∘
13∘^{\circ}∘

explanationHtml:
Given ϕ′=35∘:γsat=20kN/m3F=1.5;β=?;γ=γsat−γw\begin{aligned} \text{Given }\phi^{\prime}&=35^{\circ}: \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}=20 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ F&=1.5 ; \beta=? ; \gamma=\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \end{aligned}Given ϕ′F​=35∘:γsat​=20kN/m3=1.5;β=?;γ=γsat​−γw​​

F=γ′tan⁡ϕ′γsat tan⁡β⇒1.5=(γsat−γw)tan⁡35∘γsattan⁡β⇒tan⁡β=(20−10)tan⁡35∘1.5×20⇒β=13.14∘≃13∘ \begin{aligned} F&=\frac{\gamma^{\prime} \tan \phi^{\prime}}{\gamma_{\text {sat }} \tan \beta} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1.5&=\frac{\left(\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \tan 35^{\circ}}{\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}} \tan \beta} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \tan \beta&=\frac{(20-10) \tan 35^{\circ}}{1.5 \times 20} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \beta&=13.14^{\circ} \simeq 13^{\circ} \end{aligned}F⇒1.5⇒tanβ⇒β​=γsat ​tanβγ′tanϕ′​=γsat​tanβ(γsat​−γw​)tan35∘​=1.5×20(20−10)tan35∘​=13.14∘≃13∘​
explanationText: $\begin{aligned} \text{Given }\phi^{\prime}&=35^{\circ}: \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}=20 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ F&=1.5 ; \beta=? ; \gamma=\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \end{aligned}$ Factor of safety $\begin{aligned} F&=\frac{\gamma^{\prime} \tan \phi^{\prime}}{\gamma_{\text {sat }} \tan \beta} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1.5&=\frac{\left(\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \tan 35^{\circ}}{\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}} \tan \beta} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \tan \beta&=\frac{(20-10) \tan 35^{\circ}}{1.5 \times 20} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \beta&=13.14^{\circ} \simeq 13^{\circ} \end{aligned}$

questionText: In a triaxial test carried out on a cohesionless soil sample with a cell pressure of 20 kPa, the observed value of applied stress at the point of failure was 40 kPa. The angle of internal friction of the soil is

explanationHtml: Given,σ1=σa+σ3=40+20=60kPaNow,σ1=σ3N0+2cN2Where c=0σ1σ3=N0=6020=3=tan⁡2(45∘+ϕ2)tan⁡(45∘+ϕ2)=3=1.73245∘+ϕ2=60∘or ϕ2=60∘−45∘ϕ=30∘\begin{aligned} \text{Given,}\quad \sigma_{1} &=\sigma_{a}+\sigma_{3} \\ &=40+20=60 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \text{Now,}\quad \sigma_{1} &=\sigma_{3} N_{0}+2 \mathrm{c} \sqrt{\mathrm{N}_{2}}\\ \text{Where }\quad c&=0\\ \frac{\sigma_{1}}{\sigma_{3}} &=N_{0}=\frac{60}{20}=3 \\ &=\tan ^{2}\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\\ \tan \left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)&=\sqrt{3}=1.732 \\ 45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}&=60^{\circ} \\ \text{or }\quad \frac{\phi}{2}&=60^{\circ}-45^{\circ} \\ \phi&=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}\\Given,σ1​Now,σ1​Where cσ3​σ1​​tan(45∘+2ϕ​)45∘+2ϕ​or 2ϕ​ϕ​=σa​+σ3​=40+20=60kPa=σ3​N0​+2cN2​​=0=N0​=2060​=3=tan2(45∘+2ϕ​)=3​=1.732=60∘=60∘−45∘=30∘​
explanationText: $\begin{aligned} \text{Given,}\quad \sigma_{1} &=\sigma_{a}+\sigma_{3} \\ &=40+20=60 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \text{Now,}\quad \sigma_{1} &=\sigma_{3} N_{0}+2 \mathrm{c} \sqrt{\mathrm{N}_{2}}\\ \text{Where }\quad c&=0\\ \frac{\sigma_{1}}{\sigma_{3}} &=N_{0}=\frac{60}{20}=3 \\ &=\tan ^{2}\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\\ \tan \left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)&=\sqrt{3}=1.732 \\ 45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}&=60^{\circ} \\ \text{or }\quad \frac{\phi}{2}&=60^{\circ}-45^{\circ} \\ \phi&=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}\\$

questionText: The time for a clay layer to achieve 85% consolidation is 10 years. If the layer was half as thick, 10 times more permeable and 4 times more compressible then the time that would be required to achieve the same degree of consolidation is
explanationHtml: k=CvmvγwTv=Cvth2∴ and t1=h12Tvk1mvγw∴t2=h22Tvk2mvγwt1t2=(h1h2)2×TvTv×k2k1×mv1mv2t2t1=(h2h1)2×k1k2×mv2mv1=14×1×110×4=110t2=t110=1010=1 year \begin{aligned} k &=C_{v} m_{v} \gamma_{w} \\ T_{v} &=\frac{C_{v} t}{h^{2}} \\ \therefore \quad \text { and } \quad t_{1} &=\frac{h_{1}^{2} T_{v}}{k_{1}} m_{v} \gamma_{w} \\ \therefore \quad & t_{2}=\frac{h_{2}^{2} T_{v}}{k_{2}} m_{v} \gamma_{w} \\ & \frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}=\left(\frac{h_{1}}{h_{2}}\right)^{2} \times \frac{T_{v}}{T_{v}} \times \frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}} \times \frac{m_{v 1}}{m_{v 2}}\\ \frac{t_{2}}{t_{1}} &=\left(\frac{h_{2}}{h_{1}}\right)^{2} \times \frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}} \times \frac{m_{v 2}}{m_{v 1}} \\ &=\frac{1}{4} \times 1 \times \frac{1}{10} \times 4=\frac{1}{10} \\ t_{2} &=\frac{t_{1}}{10}=\frac{10}{10}=1 \text { year } \end{aligned}kTv​∴ and t1​∴t1​t2​​t2​​=Cv​mv​γw​=h2Cv​t​=k1​h12​Tv​​mv​γw​t2​=k2​h22​Tv​​mv​γw​t2​t1​​=(h2​h1​​)2×Tv​Tv​​×k1​k2​​×mv2​mv1​​=(h1​h2​​)2×k2​k1​​×mv1​mv2​​=41​×1×101​×4=101​=10t1​​=1010​=1 year ​

questionMarkup:
Identify the two FALSE statements from the following four statements.

I. The consolidation of soil happens due to the change in total stress.
II. When Standard Penetration Tests are performed in fine sands below the water table, the dilation correction is applied after the overburden correction is applied.
III. Over consolidated clays will have predominantly cohesive strength as compared to the frictional strength.
IV. Compaction of soils is due to expulsion of water.
questionText: Identify the two FALSE statements from the following four statements. I. The consolidation of soil happens due to the change in total stress. II. When Standard Penetration Tests are performed in fine sands below the water table, the dilation correction is applied after the overburden correction is applied. III. Over consolidated clays will have predominantly cohesive strength as compared to the frictional strength. IV. Compaction of soils is due to expulsion of water.
explanationHtml:
(I) Consolidation of soil takes place due to the change in effective stress.
(IV) Compaction of soil is due to expulsion of air.
explanationText: (I) Consolidation of soil takes place due to the change in effective stress. (IV) Compaction of soil is due to expulsion of air.

questionText: The following two statements are made with reference to the calculation of net bearing capacity of a footing in pure clay soil ( $\phi =0$ ) using Terzaghi's bearing capacity theory. Identify if they are TRUE or FALSE. I. Increase in footing width will result in increase in bearing capacity. II. Increase in depth of foundation will result in higher bearing capacity.
